digest.component_or_area: test infrastructure - subprocess and network sentinels
propositions: Five real-subprocess reap tests each burn ~1.01s wall-clock time waiting for a 1s timeout deadline to expire due to a blanket module-wide fixture that must be split into opt-in fixtures with differentiated timeouts.

Three reap tests assert on child-side setup (grandchild pidfile, spawn counter, flushed stdout) that depends on implicit timing rather than explicit readiness gates, creating a latent wall-clock race on loaded runners.

The test_run_acli_429_retries_with_rate_limit_backoff test has a latent load flake in the opposite direction: its two spawned children must complete before a 1s module-wide deadline that is now too tight.
The tight_stall fixture injects a 2s low-speed window when its sibling dribble test already proves git honors a 1s window, causing unnecessary test runtime.
Explicit readiness gates (marker files polled by parent Popen wrapper) must replace implicit timing assumptions to make ordering deterministic regardless of runner load.
